news.title: Expert sees case for both Fed rate cuts and hikes
news.summary:
STORY: "Everyone wants a strong mandate and a strong direction," said Miller, but Warsh's tight-lipped style has investors unsure of the trajectory of rates.

"It seems like the direction might be biased towards raising, but I could look at all those same indicators and say that this is an environment in which rates could come further down as well," she said. 

"When you have a single commodity driving overall prices," added Miller, referring to rising oil prices, "the point can be made that in fact rates should come down to allow consumers to continue on the path they've been on and get to the other side of the specific commodity spike."

Investors see a roughly 50% chance that the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next policy meeting in September, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
